subject: Recap & proposed smoke tests — Ava Medical discovery (next steps)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@avamed.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & proposed smoke tests — Ava Medical discovery (next steps)

Hi Linda — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our 45m discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the technical tests. Please reply with any corrections or missing items.

Call summary
- Attendees: Linda Park (Ava Medical), Evelyn Hart (Redwood), Marcus Lin (Redwood), Jordan Blake (Redwood)
- Primary pain: production latency spikes on inference (95th pct > 600ms) causing document processing timeouts; high per-token cost driving margins below target; regulatory requirement for EU data residency for some workloads.
- Current stack: self-hosted LLM endpoints on older GPU fleet + custom batching.
- Target outcomes: sub-250ms 95th latency for single-request inference; 30–40% reduction in per-token cost at parity of output quality; ability to pin EU-only routing for PHI datasets.

Decision criteria (explicit):
1) Latency at scale (95th pct <= 250ms)
2) Token cost/unit and predictable pricing for sustained throughput
3) Security & compliance (SOC2, data residency controls, KMS integration)
4) Operational observability and rollout tooling
5) Ease of integration (SDK + routing policy)

Competitive landscape noted on call
- LinguaServe: strong at structured prompts, unclear on EU-residency routing.
- CloudTensor: optimized for batch throughput but historical latency concern at low concurrency.

Proposed smoke tests (to validate criteria) — brief plan attached (redwood-smoke-test-plan.xlsx):
A) Latency baseline: run 1k single-request calls across 3 synthetic concurrency profiles (1, 5, 20) with live model variant. Measure P50/P95/P99.
B) Cost estimate run: measure token consumption and per-minute throughput to simulate steady-state 100 requests/min.
C) Resilience/fallback: induce model-variant failover and confirm automatic fallback preserves 99% availability.
D) Residency verification: deploy an EU-routed private tenant and run PHI sample inference with audit log enabled.

Open questions we asked you to confirm:
- Will you be able to provide a 10–20GB redacted sample dataset for the cost/quality runs?
- Do you need us to involve your security contact (you mentioned security@avamed.com)?
- Are there any third-party latency agents (WAFs, proxies) we should be aware of?

Next steps (suggested timeline)
- Linda: confirm dataset availability + security contact by Thu 4/22 EOD
- Redwood: finalize smoke-test workbook and provide access to test infra by Fri 4/23
- Schedule 2-hour kickoff for tests week of 4/26 (propose Tue 4/27 10:00–12:00 PT)

Attachments: redwood-smoke-test-plan.xlsx (workbook with steps and expected metrics)

Thanks — we’ll prep a short canary run script so the first 100 calls can be non-invasive.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | M: +1 (415) 555-0192

Evelyn — thank you, great summary. A few clarifications / requests from our side: 

1) Dataset: we can provide a redacted 12GB sample (clinical notes + imaging meta). We will deliver via SFTP by Thu 4/22 EOD. Please confirm preferred schema/format (CSV vs JSONL).
2) Security: yes, please loop in security@avamed.com for the residency run — they will want SOC2 docs and a short architecture diagram. Can you include SOC2 and KMS integration notes?
3) Timeline: 4/27 kickoff works for us but could we do 10:30–12:30 PT instead of 10:00? That gives our infra team buffer.

One more thing on competitors: LinguaServe flagged price floor concessions in their last RFP — we will ask for a formal price sheet. CloudTensor offered an extended free trial but would not commit to regional routing. Those are the practical points for procurement.

Thanks,
Linda
Head of Data Engineering | Ava Medical

Linda / Evelyn — technical notes from our side ahead of the kickoff: 

- Format: JSONL with one record per line is best for streaming inference — please send the sample in that format if possible. If you must provide CSV, include an id + prompt + expected_output columns.
- For the Latency baseline test we will run the following model variants: rwd-3b-ops (quantized) and rwd-7b-standard. The workbook attached will show expected CPU/GPU utilization.
- For residency: we will provision a temporary EU tenant in our Berlin region and confirm audit trail exports to your KMS during the test. We will only accept data via SFTP pull with customer-side encryption if that is your preference.
- Can your infra provide a point-of-contact for our runbook (name + pager)? We'll need someone on-call during the 2-hour kickoff.

I updated the workbook to include explicit run commands and an infra checklist (filename: redwood-smoke-test-plan.xlsx, tab: infra-checklist).
